chunks: Some of our companions, from Ibn Jamhūr, from his father, from Sulaymān ibn Samāʿah, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Qāsim, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn ʿUmar, who said:

Abū Jaʿfar al-Manṣūr sent to al-Ḥasan ibn Zayd, who was his governor over the two sanctuaries, ordering: Burn down the house of Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad. So he cast fire into the house of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, and the fire caught at the door and the corridor. Then Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام came out, stepping over the fire and walking through it.
And he was saying: I am the son of the roots of the earth; I am the son of Ibrāhīm, the Khalīl of Allah, عليه السلام.

key_terms.أَعْرَاقِ: roots or lineage, indicating ancestral origin
key_terms.النَّارَ: the fire that was cast into the house
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: the two sacred sanctuaries, meaning Makkah and al-Madīnah
key_terms.خَلِيلِ اللَّهِ: the intimate friend of Allah, a title of Prophet Ibrāhīm عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What happened when al-Manṣūr ordered the house of Imam Jaʿfar al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام to be burned?
ai.summary: This report recounts that al-Manṣūr ordered the burning of the house of Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad عليه السلام through his governor over the two sanctuaries. The Imam عليه السلام emerged through the flames unharmed while invoking his noble descent from Ibrāhīm Khalīl Allāh عليه السلام, highlighting his steadfastness and the extraordinary protection associated with the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام.
